clue.text: Seed playing can read about golf club competition

parts.note: an egg is the seed of new life, an ovum

indicators.note: about means going around, so the rearranged letters wrap the club
playing suggests the letters are played around with, rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder
a spoon is an old name for a lofted wooden golf club

explanation.surface: Someone at a golf club studies how a seeded player is doing in the club competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'golf club' looks like the venue, but a spoon is an old lofted golf club; the remaining letters of 'can read' rearrange around it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a children's sports-day race, so a type of competition.

clue.text: Novelist's grave edging, reportedly, covers passage

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits on top of, covering, the part below it
reportedly says these words are what is heard spoken rather than what is written

parts.note: grave means earnest, serious; edging means hemming, sewing a border
a way is a passage or route

explanation.surface: A writer's tombstone has a border that hides a secret passageway.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's on 'Novelist's' stands for 'is'. Said out loud, EARNEST HEMMING gives ERNEST HEMING, and in this down clue it sits over WAY.
explanation.definitionFit: The American author of The Old Man and the Sea is a famous novelist.

clue.text: Took a punt from graduate, on left-hand bank, and drifted

indicators.note: the graduate's letter stands at the left-hand edge, like a bank beside the rest

parts.note: G is a standard abbreviation for graduate
to amble is to stroll or drift along aimlessly

explanation.surface: A graduate goes punting by the left bank of the river and drifts along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took a punt' looks like boating on the Cam, but it means placed a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a punt is British slang for having a bet or a risky try.

clue.text: Celebrity touring switched to glowing religious building

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the celebrity's word encircles the rest

parts.note: a celebrity is a big name

indicators.note: switched means the two letters change places

parts.note: something glowing hot is red

explanation.surface: A famous person on tour moved over to a radiant church.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris cathedral is a celebrated religious building.

clue.text: Upset quiet soldier's expressions of dejection

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet
GI is an American soldier; with 's, GIS

explanation.surface: An upset, silent soldier shows his gloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Long audible breaths are classic outward signs of sadness or weariness.

clue.text: Performing outside in concrete area, earn encore

parts.note: a performer on stage is on

indicators.note: the outside letters found in the word concrete

parts.note: to gain is to earn

explanation.surface: A band playing outdoors on a concrete arena gets called back.
explanation.definitionFit: An encore is a repeat performance, so an adverb sense of again, one more time.

clue.text: Spirit Nicky drained with speed?

indicators.note: drained means emptied of its contents, so only the end letters remain

parts.note: MPH, miles per hour, measures speed

explanation.surface: Someone named Nicky is exhausted after a fast effort, perhaps on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests a drink to go with 'drained', but it is a nature spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth these are minor female nature deities, spirits of woods and water.

clue.text: Flier originally appears through Tim's front door half missing

indicators.note: front here puts the name's letter in front of what is left of the door
originally points to the first letter of the next word

parts.note: via means through, by way of
the opening letter of the name Tim

indicators.note: half missing means the first half of the word door is lost, leaving only its back half

explanation.surface: A pilot turns up through a door at Tim's house that is half gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A flier can be a pilot, someone who flies aircraft.

clue.text: Dog discovered outside wrong house by people here

parts.note: the clue appears in a British newspaper, so the people here are the English

indicators.note: outside means the discovered word wraps around the others

parts.note: found means discovered
a cross, X, marks a wrong answer

explanation.surface: A dog was found outside the wrong house by the locals.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a British breed of hound bred for fox hunting.

clue.text: Harry's blocked by a police force wanting ID

indicators.note: blocked by means the other letters plug its middle

parts.note: to harry is to nag; the 's stands for is
the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: Harry is stopped by the police, who want to see his identification.
explanation.definitionFit: A label worn showing who you are is a form of identification.

clue.text: English runner takes leg number six in college leisure activity

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge; a river runs
pin is slang for leg

indicators.note: the sixth letter in the word college

explanation.surface: An English athlete hurts a leg as the sixth runner in a college event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' is a crossword convention for river.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleeping in tents on holiday is a popular pastime.

clue.text: Constable aims to do such sketches of local views — Essex firstly

indicators.note: firstly asks for the first letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: The painter John Constable set out to draw sketches of local scenery around Essex.
explanation.walkthrough: John Constable painted the Essex-Suffolk border; here a constable is a police officer who aims to crack crimes.
explanation.definitionFit: A police constable's goal is to clear up, resolve, cases.

clue.text: Italian serving special crackers at eight

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: An Italian waiter serves special crackers at eight o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Long thin pasta is a dish from Italy, a portion served there.

clue.text: Short water pipe, say, is placed over a shrubby plant

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, losing its last letter

parts.note: a hydrant is a street water outlet pipe

indicators.note: placed over means turned over, so the two letters are flipped

parts.note: EG, for example, means say

explanation.surface: A short hosepipe is laid over a flowering shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering garden shrub with large rounded heads of blooms.

clue.text: Place to eat and chat about Proust novel

indicators.note: about means round, so the chat word goes around the rest

parts.note: gab means chat

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A literary pub evening discussing a Proust novel over dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub serving good food is a dining venue.

clue.text: Size of waist perhaps taking cook aback (disheartening truth)

indicators.note: aback means backwards, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: to cook the books is to rig them

indicators.note: removing the heart, the middle, leaves only the outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone is taken aback by the disheartening truth about their waistline after cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Girth is a measurement round the middle, of which waist size is an example.

clue.text: Old ruler has two thousand pounds to entertain brothers on river

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold within, so the brothers and river go inside

parts.note: a grand is a thousand pounds, and K is another thousand

indicators.note: in a down clue on means sitting above

parts.note: union members call each other brothers; TU is trade union

explanation.surface: An old monarch spends two thousand pounds hosting his brothers on a river trip.
explanation.definitionFit: This title was given to the Ottoman sultan, a historical ruler.

clue.text: Film second contest

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
to vie is to contest

explanation.surface: A film is entered for a second competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A movie is the American word for a cinema picture, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Practical workers united in repairing rail, after five

indicators.note: after means the rest of the wordplay follows the numeral

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five

indicators.note: in means placed inside the rebuilt letters
repairing means putting the letters back together in a new way

parts.note: TU, trade union, is workers united

explanation.surface: Union workers are fixing a railway line after five o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Practical' here means in effect, as in a virtual certainty.
explanation.definitionFit: Something virtual is so in practice or in effect, though not formally.

clue.text: Country health farm signior regularly attended after damage

indicators.note: after means the picked letters follow the damage word

parts.note: a san is a sanatorium, a health resort
to mar is to damage

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter

explanation.surface: An Italian gentleman goes to a health spa regularly after an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny republic inside Italy is a sovereign state.

clue.text: Embryonic design of iron enthrals university type extremely

indicators.note: enthrals means captivates, holds inside
a design of the letters means a new arrangement of them
the extremes are the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A designer's iron work holds a university type spellbound.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means within the womb, the stage of an embryo.

clue.text: Visor on ground restricts team game — there's trouble catching

indicators.note: restricts means hems in, so the game goes inside
ground means crushed, so the letters are broken up and remade

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a team game

explanation.surface: A rugby player's visor falls on the pitch during a game, and there's trouble catching the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' reads as fielding a ball, but here means contagious.
explanation.definitionFit: A stomach bug that is highly contagious is a catching illness, a trouble one can pick up.

clue.text: Recording number six: poem, start to finish

parts.note: VI is Roman six

indicators.note: the first letter is moved to the end

parts.note: an ode is a poem

explanation.surface: A recording of the sixth poem from start to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A filmed tape or file is a recording.

clue.text: Sloth perhaps displayed excellent mount

parts.note: sloth is one of the seven deadly sins
A1 means excellent, written AI

explanation.surface: A sloth was shown off on a fine mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sloth' suggests the animal (an ai is in fact a sloth), but it is the deadly sin.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical mountain where Moses received the commandments; mount is a mountain.

clue.text: Maybe change fleece that's awful

parts.note: to fleece or do someone is to swindle them
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Perhaps exchange a fleece that's horrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Dough is slang for money, of which loose change is an example.

clue.text: Injury intensified having pulled someone's leg

parts.note: a wound is an injury
up means raised, intensified, as in turning the volume up

explanation.surface: An injury got worse after someone was tripped by the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind someone up is British slang for teasing them, so the past form means having teased.

clue.text: New type of light seen during Christmas, mostly gold

indicators.note: seen during means placed within the trimmed festive word
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: Noel is Christmas
UV, ultraviolet, is a type of light
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A new kind of light appears at Christmas, mainly golden.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for new is used in English, as in nouveau riche.

clue.text: A way to get rich? Fearful woman in US describes twist

parts.note: yellow means cowardly, fearful

indicators.note: describes means draws round, so the woman's word encircles the twist

parts.note: broad is American slang for a woman
a rick is a wrench or twist of a joint

explanation.surface: Is there a route to wealth? A nervous American woman describes a plot twist.
explanation.walkthrough: The road in The Wizard of Oz led to the Emerald City; the question mark flags the fanciful link to wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: The gold-coloured road suggests a path to riches, playing on a cliched route to wealth.
